lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing, Python
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The current mechanic role makes the product-career direction and transition unclear.
items.because: Recruiters may wonder whether you are pursuing product roles and what led to the change.

items.says: Give the product internship and food-rescue app more prominence.
items.because: They are the strongest product credentials but are interrupted by the current role outside product.

items.says: Add a brief product-focused summary near the top.
items.because: Without one, readers must infer your direction from the timeline.

items.says: Standardize units and metric presentation across the page.
Check that the profile link works and points to a professional profile.
Consider adding a location.
items.because: It can help with roles that have location or relocation constraints.

items.says: Assess how much space the engine-rebuild bullet deserves.
items.because: It is less directly relevant to product applications than the product experience.

items.says: Make sure the under-five-days claim is representative and its timeframe is clear.
The hydraulic-systems bullet has no outcome and may be lower priority.
items.because: It has less impact than the first mechanic bullet.

items.says: Clarify which merchants the 9-to-4-day result covers.
items.because: The boundary between the pilot region and later rollout is unclear.

items.says: Express the conversion change in percentage points.
items.because: The reader currently has to infer the size of the change.

items.says: Distinguish the tested population from the rollout scope.
Explain how support tickets closed served as a proxy for RICE Reach.
items.because: Reach generally concerns users or customers affected over a defined period.

items.says: Clarify how the rest of the RICE framework was applied.
items.because: The bullet mentions only Reach.

items.says: Make the main contribution and resulting decision or impact easier to identify.
items.because: The bullet packs discovery, analysis, business-case work, and a decision together.

items.says: The checkout A/B test duplicates the earlier checkout-conversion bullet.
items.because: The same experiment is given two bullets.

items.says: Clarify what was measured and what the reported lift represents.
items.because: The phrase about the effect on merchants’ customers is unclear.

items.says: Make the funded rollout the central outcome.
items.because: That would keep the bullet distinct from the onboarding result.

items.says: Clarify what “funded” means.
items.because: It could be read in more than one way.

items.says: Make the scorecard work’s connection to a product role more explicit.
items.because: The result supports a product profile through data-informed decisions, but the connection is not stated.

items.says: Add the measurement period for the pick-error reduction, if available.
Clarify how the slotting changes relate to the 30% reduction.
Clarify the consensus forecast’s relationship to the reduction in forecast error.
Separate or prioritize the route-planning contributions.
items.because: The bullet combines rollout, SOP changes, training, vendor negotiations, and time saved.

items.says: Clarify which actions drove the savings and which were your direct ownership.
items.because: The combined account makes both difficult to tell.

items.says: Explain how the 1,800 driver hours were calculated or attributed.
Distinguish the potential audience of 3,100 students from actual users.
Make the one-year measurement period for the food total clear.
Calling growth from 400 to 1,150 weekly active users a 150% increase is incorrect.
items.because: It is a 187.5% increase.

items.says: Make sure the weekly-active-user measurement periods are comparable.
Clarify how the interviews connected to the reminder feature.
Calling the rise from 75% to 95% a 20% increase uses the wrong unit.
items.because: It is a 20-percentage-point rise.

items.says: Explain the volunteer system’s role in the fill-rate result if it can be substantiated.
Distinguish the modeled $2.4M opportunity from realized savings.
items.because: Readers could mistake the estimate for savings already achieved.

items.says: Replace the passive account with a clearer statement of your contribution.
Clarify what changed or was adopted and report a meaningful result if available.
items.because: The bullet has no measurable result and may be lower priority without one.

items.says: The pilot-approval outcome repeats the savings bullet.
items.because: The approval is already mentioned there.

items.says: Make broad product skills such as roadmapping and requirements writing more specific or supported by experience.
items.because: Broad skills are harder to evaluate.

items.says: Indicate the kind or level of Python work you can perform if relevant.
items.because: The skill should not imply proficiency beyond actual use.

items.says: Show what you use Excel for.
items.because: Excel is broad, and the résumé does not show its use.
